attractions.name: Moola Chotok waterfall
attractions.description: A dramatic waterfall in a rocky gorge near Khuzdar, considered one of Balochistan's most scenic natural spots.

attractions.name: Khuzdar bazaars
attractions.description: Local markets known for Balochi handicrafts, embroidery, and regional goods.

transportation.notes: Regular daily departures along the N-25 highway
Long route; check current road conditions

accommodations.name: Mid-range hotel near the main bazaar

weather_info.climate_type: Semi-arid mountain climate, milder than the Balochistan plains due to elevation

travel_tips.tip: Khuzdar sits directly on the N-25 highway, making it a natural stopover between Quetta and Karachi.
Hire a local taxi for the Moola Chotok waterfall trip, as it's off the main highway and best reached with a local driver.
Check current travel advisories before road travel through this region, particularly for longer overland routes.
Visit Moola Chotok outside the summer months when water flow and temperatures are both more pleasant.

history.founded: An old settlement with roots as a trading post along historic caravan routes
history.city_history: Khuzdar has long served as a trading and administrative center for central Balochistan, positioned along key routes connecting Quetta to the coast. Today it's known regionally for the dramatic Moola Chotok waterfall nearby.
history.province_history: Balochistan is Pakistan's largest province by area, historically home to various Baloch and Pashtun tribal confederacies, and was governed as British Balochistan before its princely states acceded to Pakistan between 1947 and 1948.
